Diagram: phone on a steady stand, two to three metres away from the athlete, who is side-on to it
Place the phone 2 to 3 metres away, at about waist height.
Keep the phone completely still. Lean it on something or ask someone to hold it steady.
Stand or lie side-on to the phone, with your whole body visible from head to feet.
Use a bright place. Avoid standing with a window or the sun behind you.
Top: sit all the way up
Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Sit all the way up until your chest is close to your knees.
Lie all the way back down before the next one.
Do as many as you can until the time ends.
A sit-up counts only if you sit all the way up and lie all the way back. Half sit-ups are not counted.
Stand completely still during the 3-2-1 countdown. This lets the app measure your height.
Jump straight up as high as you can.
Land on the same spot where you started.
You may jump more than once. Your best jump counts.
Do not step towards or away from the phone during the test — the measurement will be wrong and the attempt will not count.
Lie down side-on to the camera with your whole body visible. Sit all the way up each time.
Stand side-on, whole body in view. Stay still for the countdown, then jump.
The app needs your camera to record the test. The video is sent only to SAI.

Stand side-on to the camera with your whole body visible. Go down until your thighs are level, then stand all the way up.
Get into a plank side-on to the camera with your whole body visible. Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Stand facing the camera with your upper body and hips visible. Keep your elbows by your sides.
Stand side-on to the camera with your whole body visible. Bend both knees until they are close to a right angle.
Stand facing the phone, with your head, arms and hips visible.
Bottom: thighs level with the ground
Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and push your hips back until your thighs are level with the ground.
Stand all the way back up before the next one.
A squat counts only if you go down until your thighs are level and stand all the way back up. Half squats are not counted.
Bottom: chest close to the ground
Start in a plank: hands under your shoulders, arms straight, body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows until your chest is close to the ground.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
A push-up counts only if you go all the way down and up with your body straight. Push-ups with sagging or raised hips are not counted.
Top: hand up to the shoulder
Stand tall with your arms straight down and your elbows against your sides.
Bend one elbow and bring your hand up to your shoulder.
Lower it until your arm is straight again.
Use the same arm for every curl. A curl counts only if you go all the way up and down with your elbow by your side.
Stand tall. Take a long step forward with one foot.
Bend both knees until your back knee is close to the ground.
Push back up until both legs are straight.
A lunge counts only if both knees bend far enough and you stand back up. Keep your feet well apart — bending with your feet together is not a lunge.
Do as many as you can with good form until the time ends.
